about: The reference agenda and presenter script (docs/07-agenda-and-script-guide.md), as slides. Written by hand from the board as it stood on 2026-11-12. Per slide: `slide` (title, content, activity, results, text, meme), `section`, `cue` (one line on screen), `cards` (posts and news as cards; sides and notes as plain text), and `prep` (the presenter's notes, only on their own phone and in rehearsal). `activities` name their activity slide in `segment`. Load with scripts/apply-agenda.mjs; `ask` is computed there, never stored here.

agenda.title: November guild meeting
agenda.detail: A word cloud on phones, then a post on voice-driven coding and the tricks on your screen.
agenda.cue: Phones out: open GuildBoard and join the room.

points: Wait until the room count passes ten before you move on.
Guests can join with just a name. Nobody’s answers are ever shown with names.
prep.opener: Morning, guild. Phones out: open GuildBoard, tap the banner, you’re in. Everything today happens there.

agenda.title: The tool you’d refuse to give up
agenda.cue: One word. Editor, terminal, shortcut, mug: all of it counts.

points: Wait for ten-odd words, then close it. Don’t discuss it yet.
Close moves to the results by itself.
prep.opener: One word on your phone: the tool you’d refuse to give up. Editor, terminal, a shortcut, a mug. All of it counts.

agenda.title: Your desk, in words
agenda.cue: Biggest word wins. Who’s the holdout?

points: There’s always one. Let them defend it for thirty seconds.
Small words count too: read one odd one out, it gets a laugh.
prep.opener: Read the biggest word aloud. If one editor owns the cloud, who’s the holdout?

agenda.title: Steal a trick
agenda.cue: Dictating code yet? Where did it fall apart?

points: Ask where it fell apart: naming things, punctuation, the open-plan office.
Got a trick on your screen? A volunteer shares it, two minutes, no slides. Never ask anyone by name.
prep.opener: Simon Willison built a feature for his blog almost entirely by voice. Anyone here dictating code yet?

panels.label: After
panels.text: The keys were as small as 4.

meme.caption: Trust, but check the key size.

agenda.title: Who do we trust with our code?
agenda.detail: eMudhra CA compromise · GLM-5.3 KV-cache leak on Workers AI · Google’s AI gaming platform (a member’s link). Then a poll.
agenda.cue: Let’s explore.

points: Don’t read the cards out. One line each, then straight to the vote.
prep.opener: Three stories from this month. Two of them are someone else’s infrastructure failing quietly.

agenda.title: This month’s Radar
agenda.cue: Tap one on your phone to read it.

cards.title: eMudhra intermediate CA compromise
cards.why: Keys as small as 4 let private keys be recovered from public certificates.

cards.title: GLM-5.3 on Workers AI leaked KV cache between users
cards.why: A context-window mismatch let cache pages cross between users’ requests.

cards.title: Google experiments with an AI-powered gaming platform
cards.why: Posted to the Radar by a member.

points: The fix for GLM-5.3: make the memory pool limits match the model’s config.
The Google link is a member’s: thank them, and ask for more links like it.
prep.opener: eMudhra: Cloudflare found keys as small as 4. GLM-5.3: cache pages crossed between users.

agenda.title: Production code to a hosted AI model?
agenda.cue: Vote on your phone.

points: Counts show after 8 seconds, so the first votes don’t steer the rest.
prep.opener: Vote now: would you send production code to a hosted AI model?

agenda.title: Who do we trust?
agenda.cue: Smallest camp: defend it.

points: Then ask the biggest camp what would change their mind. A leak like GLM-5.3’s?
prep.opener: Smallest camp, you’re up: defend it in one line.

agenda.title: The tech vs the business
agenda.detail: From the board, posted anonymously: the host frames it. Poll, then the debate: what it changes about the tools we pick.
agenda.cue: A crash in AI stocks isn’t AI going away. Or is it?

points: The post’s split: the tech is useful and improving; the risk is spending with no clear way to earn it back.
Dot-com is the template: plenty of companies died, the internet didn’t.
prep.opener: From the board, posted anonymously: AI stocks crashing is not AI going away. Or is it?

agenda.title: AI by 2028?
agenda.cue: Vote before you overthink it.

points: Close it once most of the room has voted.
prep.opener: Vote before you overthink it: does AI pop by 2028?

agenda.title: AI by 2028
agenda.cue: Which tool you use every day disappears first if it pops?

points: Ask the “pops” camp which AI vendor they’d bet on surviving, and why.
prep.opener: Which tool you use every day disappears first if it pops?

agenda.title: Your main AI tool doubles its price next quarter.
agenda.cue: What’s the plan? One concrete answer beats ten opinions.

points: Push for one concrete answer: a fallback, a self-hosted model, going without.
Write the best answer down as a note. It may be a decision.
prep.opener: Your main AI tool doubles its price or shuts down next quarter. What’s the plan?

agenda.title: Name the blocker
agenda.detail: No problem posts on the board, so a word cloud of one-word blockers; the two biggest get three minutes each.
agenda.cue: No problem posts this month, so the room sets the agenda.

points: Next slide opens the word cloud by itself.
prep.opener: No problem posts on the board this month, so you set the agenda.

agenda.title: What slowed you down most this month?
agenda.cue: One word. Nobody sees who typed what.

points: Close it when the words stop moving.
prep.opener: One word: what slowed you down most this month? Builds, reviews, flaky tests, waiting on access.

agenda.title: This month’s blockers
agenda.cue: Top two get three minutes each. One owner, one next step.

points: Don’t solve it live: one owner and one next step per blocker, as a decision note.
Bigger than three minutes? It goes on next month’s board as a problem post.
prep.opener: Take the biggest word. Who hit this last week, and what did you try?

agenda.title: Data structures in unexpected places
agenda.detail: From the board, posted anonymously: Git history as a linked list, MongoDB indexes as B-trees, the Kubernetes scheduler’s priority queue.
agenda.cue: Name one hiding in a tool we use. Chat counts.

points: Unmuting is optional: answers in the call chat count. Read the first two aloud.
If nobody bites: where did we reach for a plain list or map and later wish we hadn’t?
prep.opener: Git history is a linked list. Mongo indexes are B-trees. The Kubernetes scheduler is a priority queue. Name one you’ve caught hiding in a tool we use.

panels.label: The interview
panels.text: Implement a B-tree on the whiteboard.

agenda.title: Kers’ Boss Round
agenda.detail: Sum of the even numbers, in JavaScript, in your own browser. The screen shows only the % who pass: no names, no code.
agenda.cue: You lot tell me what to write all day. Let’s see if you can still code.

points: Your code stays on your device. The screen shows only the pass rate.
Admins play too, presenter included.
prep.opener: You lot tell me what to write all day. Let’s see if you can still code.

agenda.title: sumEvens(nums)
agenda.cue: On your phone or laptop. Run the tests as often as you like.

points: When most of the room has had a go, close the round: Kers gives his verdict next.
prep.opener: Six tests, empty arrays and negatives included. Run them as often as you like.

agenda.title: Kers’ verdict
agenda.cue: What tripped you: the empty array or the negatives?

points: Over half? Ask the first to pass what they wrote. Chat counts.
prep.opener: Under half passing? Ask the room what tripped them: the empty array or the negatives.

agenda.title: Before you go
agenda.detail: Decisions and owners from the notes, and one Radar link each.
agenda.cue: One line: what will you actually try this week?

points: Read the decision notes back with their owners. No owner? Assign it or drop it.
This month’s Radar was mostly the digest: one link each.
prep.opener: Before you go: what’s one thing from today you’ll actually try this week? Chat or mic, one line.

agenda.title: Rate today’s meeting
agenda.cue: Vote on your phone. Be honest.

agenda.title: How did we do?
agenda.cue: Thanks for being honest. We read every one.

agenda.title: Thanks, guild.
agenda.cue: Two minutes: fill the guild survey. Scan the code or tap the button.

activities.prompt: The tool you’d refuse to give up
Would you send production code to a hosted AI model?
One word: what slowed you down most this month?
